headline: Today or nothing: work the cool west corner early
body:
Today is your only window. The channel zone starts light — NW 5–10, seas 2–4 ft, the triangle midday near 3.8 ft — but W wind fills to 10–20 by afternoon, gusting into the low teens at the grounds. Go early and be running home by early afternoon. Monday is out: a small-craft advisory hits the channel Monday afternoon, and the triangle builds to 5 ft with NW 18–29 kn, gusting 35. A blowout, worse on the outer banks.

Straight talk on the break: it isn't in the triangle. All three corners read warm — east (Anacapa) 73.5, south point 72.6, west (Santa Cruz) coolest at 71.1. Nothing near the 64–68 band. Start the west corner and work its cool edge, but temper hopes; the true break has slid off toward Santa Rosa Flats, where tomorrow drops to 67.3 — and that ground is unreachable, 7-ft seas and 23–30 kn NW. Osborn and San Nicolas sit warm in the 73s and windy. Not worth the run.
